Messages.Author: Sam Bartels
Messages.Body:
Oh yeah, could any replies to this one or the paralyze question be sent
via e-mail, thanks!

This is how I understand the voting situation. Correct me if I am wrong
ANYWHERE!

A vampire does a political action (using a card which is replaced at the
end of the turn) at +1 stealth, which taps the acting vampire. If the
action is blocked the card is burned (and then replaced! since political
action cards are not replaced until the end of a POLITICAL action, but it
does not say "do not replace until the end of combat"), and combat
ensues. If the action is not blocked the acting methuselah gets 1 vote
for the action. Then, each methuselah can also cast votes for the titles
of their READY vampires (not in torpor). Then, each methuselah can cast a
vote for each political action card he or she has in their hand for each
vampire that they have ready that did not vote via a title (which are not
replaced). For example: my predator calls a vote; I have three ready
vampires, one of which is a primogen (2 tapped and one untapped - it
DOESN'T matter); I have 5 political action cards in my hand; I can cast
only 3 votes - 1 for the primogen, and 2 for the other two vampires (which
does not tap untapped vampires).

Is this how it goes?

Check it all please, but the main question is can you cast as many votes
as you have political cards in your hand, independent of how many vampires
you have ready (even if you have ZERO vampires ready).

Sam

>Then, each methuselah can also cast votes for the titles
>of their READY vampires (not in torpor).

technically correct, but poorly worded. a methuselah may choose to gain a
number of votes for each ready titled vampire he or she controls: one for
primogens, two for princes, three for justicars.

>Then, each methuselah can cast a
>vote for each political action card he or she has in their hand for each
>vampire that they have ready that did not vote via a title (which are not
>replaced).

wholly incorrect. untitled vampires normally have no effect on political
actions at all, barring certain presence or dominate reaction cards (or
action modifiers).

>For example: my predator calls a vote; I have three ready
>vampires, one of which is a primogen (2 tapped and one untapped - it
>DOESN'T matter); I have 5 political action cards in my hand; I can cast
>only 3 votes - 1 for the primogen, and 2 for the other two vampires (which
>does not tap untapped vampires).

to clarify your somewhat confused example: your predator calls a vote. you
have a primogen and two untitled vampires ready, and five political action
cards in your hand. you have six votes available, one from the primogen,
and five from burning political cards in your hand. casting votes does not
tap, untap, tickle, or bleach a vampire, barring certain action modifiers.

>Is this how it goes?

nope. read the rules.

>Check it all please, but the main question is can you cast as many votes
>as you have political cards in your hand, independent of how many vampires
>you have ready (even if you have ZERO vampires ready).

yes. go home, read the rules, and don't bother the group again until you've
grown a clue; the rules on voting are fairly clear in the rules text.

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Sam Bartels <sam.b...@diamond.gslis.ucla.edu> wrote:
>A vampire does a political action (using a card which is replaced at the
>end of the turn) at +1 stealth, which taps the acting vampire. If the
>action is blocked the card is burned (and then replaced! since political
>action cards are not replaced until the end of a POLITICAL action, but it
>does not say "do not replace until the end of combat"), and combat
>ensues. If the action is not blocked the acting methuselah gets 1 vote
>for the action. Then, each methuselah can also cast votes for the titles
>of their READY vampires (not in torpor). Then, each methuselah can cast a
>vote for each political action card he or she has in their hand for each
>vampire that they have ready that did not vote via a title (which are not
>replaced). For example: my predator calls a vote; I have three ready
>vampires, one of which is a primogen (2 tapped and one untapped - it
>DOESN'T matter); I have 5 political action cards in my hand; I can cast
>only 3 votes - 1 for the primogen, and 2 for the other two vampires (which
>does not tap untapped vampires).

If a card in hand was used to start the political action,
then that card is replaced immediately, just like any other action card.
The rule is that cards are not replaced during a vote, not "during a
political action." For example, cards are not replaced during a bloodhunt
vote, which would not be true if the rule was "during a political action".

There are several sources of votes: titled vampires, cards in hand, the
edge, Ventrue Headquarters, and so on. Any and all of these can be used
during a vote, even if casting those votes wouldn't change the verdict at
the moment. They can be used in any order desired. When you burn a political
card in hand for a vote, it is the player burning a card, not a vampire,
so it doesn't matter whether you have any ready vampires. A vampire can get
any votes from any number of sources, but can only use a given reaction or
action modifier once.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@hal.com Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

In general, the way we play you would just put the card you pulled back on
the top of your deck, since you would get the card nice time you draw anyway.

However, this could be prevented by the fact that you do not re-draw the
card until the action is complete (well, not complete, but at least started)
since I believe you cannot draw here (i.e. drawing a stealth card and then
using it to increase stealth--not sure if you can do that), and therefore
the action would get taken back, you would take back your card, and never
pick up the top card.

Matt the Tired (Justicar)

Messages.Body:
Before I could do anything to stop it, matt...@utdallas.edu wrote:

> talking about above (that I can't remember the name of) can still be used

If memory serves (I don't have my rules with me), you don't replace
political cards until the political action is finished. This means that
either a) the vote was blocked, or b) the vote was completed. When you
play that vote action, you don't replace the card immediately (which
might let you draw another vote card). That way you have plenty of room
in your hand if the voting action is cancelled.

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Any political action card used to start a political action is replaced
immediately, as are any action modifiers or reactions played while it's
being determined whether the action will be blocked. Only if the vote
actually begins is card replacement put on hold.


Messages.Author: Brian Wilson
Messages.Body:
Before I could do anything to stop it, Tom Wylie wrote:

> Any political action card used to start a political action is replaced
> immediately, as are any action modifiers or reactions played while it's
> being determined whether the action will be blocked. Only if the vote
> actually begins is card replacement put on hold.

Here in section 17.1 of the rules it says the following:

"When a political card is played as an action or a call for a bloodhunt
against a vampire committing diablerie, a vote is called. A vote is always
yes or no. A political card always provides one vote for the Methusela
playing it. Note that no cards played during a vote are replaced until
after the vote.

"Additional political cards can also be used by any of the other
Methuselahs for votes. The actual effects of these cards are ignored.
Cards used in this way are discarded to the ash heap, but, as stated, not
replaced until the voting is finished."

Note the reference to "additional political cards," which includes the
original political card in the grouping of cards not replaced. They
probably should have printed, "Do not replace until after the political
action is completed" on the cards like they did with some combat cards.

A vote is a vote until it's blocked, so it looks like no cards would be
replaced until it's successfully blocked or successfully completed. Is
there a design team ruling that says you replace the original action card
immediately? My quote is from the revised rules.
